metadata.condition_name: Sporadic hemiplegic migraine with reversible MRI changes and focal motor seizures
metadata.difficulty_description: Moderate difficulty due to MRI showing diffuse cortical swelling and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity (concerning for ischemia or encephalitis) with simultaneously normal DWI. Focal motor seizures complicate the picture (migralepsy consideration). Sporadic hemiplegic migraine diagnosis requires systematic exclusion of acute infarction, MELAS, epilepsy, and autoimmune causes.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Diagnostic puzzle: hemiplegic migraine with migralepsy and reversible MRI changes — extensive mimic exclusion (MELAS, encephalitis, primary epilepsy, stroke)
case_body_concerns: Required tool(s) lacking initial or followup outputs in the case body — agent calling them will fall back to off-pathway tier or empty result; tools: ['search_medical_literature (only fallback)']

patient.presenting_complaint: Left-sided throbbing headache with right arm weakness, speech difficulty, and a witnessed shaking episode
patient.hpi: A 26-year-old woman presented to the emergency department brought by her partner with a 3-hour history of severe left-sided throbbing headache that began approximately 30 minutes after she developed blurred vision in her right visual field. Shortly after the headache peaked, her partner noticed that she was struggling to find words and her right arm appeared weak. Within the following hour she experienced two brief episodes of right-hand rhythmic jerking lasting approximately 90 seconds each, during which she was unresponsive, followed by postictal confusion lasting approximately 20 minutes. She has had episodes of unilateral throbbing headache accompanied by transient arm weakness affecting alternating sides since the age of 14. During those earlier attacks, the weakness has always resolved completely within a few hours, and previous assessments including head CT, brain MRI, MR angiography, lumbar puncture, and basic metabolic and mitochondrial blood tests were all documented as normal at age 17 and again at age 22. She was commenced on topiramate 75 mg twice daily approximately two years ago following inadequate response to flunarizine; despite this she continues to have one to two attacks monthly. There is no family history of similar episodes, hemiplegic migraine, or any neurological condition. She does not smoke, drinks alcohol only occasionally, and uses no illicit substances. She takes topiramate and a combined oral contraceptive pill (Mercilon, desogestrel 150 mcg / ethinylestradiol 20 mcg). She has no known drug allergies.
pmh: Sporadic hemiplegic migraine — diagnosed age 22, ICHD-3 1.2.3

medications.indication: Contraception — WHO Category 4 — must be stopped

family_history: No family history of hemiplegic migraine, stroke, or neurological disease. Mother has tension-type headache.

social_history.note: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol (1-2 units/week), no illicit drugs. Lives with partner. Works as teaching assistant. Not pregnant.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, mildly confused, oriented to person and place but not time. Motor aphasia — single word responses, no paraphasic errors. Follows simple one-step commands.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Visual fields by confrontation: mild right homonymous visual field restriction that patient reports is improving from earlier. Pupils 4mm equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Fundoscopy normal. Facial symmetry slightly reduced on right with right lower facial droop. Tongue protruded midline.
neurological_exam.motor: Right upper extremity: power 3/5 throughout. Right lower extremity: power 4/5. Left upper and lower extremity: power 5/5. Tone normal bilaterally.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Brisk throughout. Right plantar extensor (Babinski positive). Left plantar flexor.
neurological_exam.sensation: Intact to light touch and pinprick bilaterally. No cortical sensory deficits.
neurological_exam.coordination: Limited on right due to weakness. Left cerebellar tests intact.
neurological_exam.gait: Not assessed — patient was bed-bound at presentation.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch and pinprick bilaterally. No cortical sensory deficits.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Sporadic hemiplegic migraine (ICHD-3 1.2.3) with migralepsy (single seizure during aura, ICHD-3 1.4.4) and reversible MRI changes — comprehensive workup excluded structural and metabolic mimics

differential.key_features: Genetic panel pending; sporadic and familial forms are clinically indistinguishable in isolated cases

differential.diagnosis: Focal motor seizure with secondary aphasia and post-ictal Todd's paralysis
differential.key_features: Witnessed shaking episode raises seizure question; migralepsy (seizure occurring during migraine aura) is the most parsimonious explanation when EEG shows no ongoing epileptiform activity
No family history, normal lactate, normal m.3243A>G; reversible MRI changes can mimic MELAS lesions
MRA normal, reversible MRI changes argue against permanent infarct

optimal_actions.action: Search guideline literature to confirm ICHD-3 1.2 criteria for migraine with aura and exclude SNOOP/CHATS red flags
optimal_actions.expected_finding: ICHD-3 criteria for migraine with aura confirmed; no SNOOP red flag present that mandates further workup

tool_parameters.query: ICHD-3 migraine with aura diagnostic criteria SNOOP red flags

optimal_actions.action: Check drug interactions and contraindications for acute (triptan/ergotamine/CGRP antagonist) and prophylactic (beta-blocker, topiramate, valproate, amitriptyline) migraine medications appropriate to this patient
optimal_actions.expected_finding: TRIPTANS AND ERGOTAMINES CONTRAINDICATED in hemiplegic migraine; OCP safety review; AED choice if seizure recurs

optimal_actions.action: Repeat brain MRI at 48h and follow-up to document reversibility
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reversible cortical / subcortical signal changes over 48h to weeks — consistent with hemiplegic migraine; no new infarct

optimal_actions.action: EEG to evaluate for ongoing epileptiform activity
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No interictal epileptiform activity; possible focal slowing during/after the migralepsy episode

optimal_actions.action: Mitochondrial / autoimmune workup and genetic panel for hemiplegic migraine
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal lactate; negative autoimmune encephalitis panel; CACNA1A / ATP1A2 / SCN1A pending

optimal_actions.action: Lumbar puncture given encephalopathy-like features and to exclude infectious / autoimmune cause
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal CSF — no pleocytosis, normal protein/glucose; supports exclusion of encephalitis

useless_tools.rationale: Head CT is less sensitive than MRI for migraine-relevant structural causes and is not indicated in typical migraine with aura; even when imaging is warranted, MRI is preferred
Routine ECG is not indicated for migraine workup; only a baseline ECG to screen triptan contraindications in patients with cardiovascular risk factors has any role
Routine transthoracic / bubble echocardiogram (PFO screening) is NOT indicated in migraine with aura; PFO-migraine association is controversial and PFO closure does not reduce migraine [Charles_2017]
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated in typical migraine with aura — no role unless cardioembolic stroke is on the differential

critical_actions: Confirm hemiplegic migraine — fully reversible motor aura plus visual / sensory / speech aura
Document seizure with EEG and consider AED if recurrence (migralepsy is a recognised ICHD-3 entity)
Confirm MRI changes reversible on follow-up imaging
Avoid triptans and ergotamines in hemiplegic migraine
Re-evaluate OCP if patient is on combined OCP
contraindicated_actions: Do not prescribe triptans or ergotamines in hemiplegic migraine
Do not start combined oestrogen-progestogen contraception
Do not commit to long-term AED on the basis of a single migralepsy seizure
key_reasoning_points: Migralepsy (ICHD-3 1.4.4) is a seizure triggered by migraine aura — requires aura to be temporally followed by a seizure
Reversible MRI signal changes are recognised in hemiplegic migraine and should not be misinterpreted as permanent infarct
Hemiplegic migraine workup must exclude MELAS, autoimmune encephalitis, and structural causes

red_herrings.intended_effect: May anchor on primary epilepsy diagnosis
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Single seizure during aura is migralepsy, not chronic epilepsy; EEG normalises interictally

red_herrings.intended_effect: May suggest infarct, encephalitis, or MELAS
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Reversible signal changes on follow-up imaging are characteristic of hemiplegic migraine

red_herrings.data_point: Two focal right-sided motor seizures during the attack
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Seizures are migralepsy — focal seizures triggered by hemiplegic migraine aura, not a primary epileptic disorder. EEG showed no epileptiform discharges or hemispheric dysfunction. The MRI abnormalities (cortical swelling, FLAIR signal) are reversible and DWI-negative, inconsistent with post-ictal changes from status epilepticus.

red_herrings.data_point: Diffuse left hemispheric cortical swelling and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Critically, DWI is normal, CSF shows no pleocytosis, autoimmune antibody panels negative, HSV PCR negative. Reversibility on 72-hour follow-up MRI confirms CSD-mediated cortical hyperaemia in hemiplegic migraine.

red_herrings.data_point: Current use of combined OCP (Mercilon EE 20 mcg)
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: MRV would show no sinus thrombosis. DWI is normal excluding arterial infarction. However, OCP is WHO Category 4 in hemiplegic migraine and must be stopped, even though it is not the cause of this acute attack — this is a critical management action the agent must identify.

signal_characteristics.FLAIR: gyral cortical hyperintensity with sulcal effacement

findings.mass_effect: mild sulcal effacement left hemisphere — consistent with vasogenic oedema
findings.borders: diffuse, non-territorial, no vascular territory demarcation

findings.location: circle of Willis and major cerebral arteries

signal_characteristics.MRA: patent bilateral ICA, MCA, ACA, PCA, basilar; no occlusion, stenosis, or dissection; no arterial filling defect

mri.impression: 1. Diffuse left hemispheric cortical swelling with T2/FLAIR gyral cortical hyperintensity and mild sulcal effacement. 2. Critically, DWI is NORMAL — no restricted diffusion, no cytotoxic oedema. No leptomeningeal or cortical enhancement. 3. Normal MRA — no arterial occlusion, stenosis, or dissection. The pattern of vasogenic cortical oedema without cytotoxic oedema and non-territorial distribution does not conform to an arterial infarct. Imaging differential includes cortical spreading depression, autoimmune encephalitis, and other causes of cortical vasogenic oedema. Follow-up MRI is recommended to assess reversibility

background.pdr: 6-7 Hz theta-range activity bilaterally — post-ictal slowing
background.overall: mild diffuse slowing consistent with post-ictal state; no hemispheric asymmetry

findings.morphology: Mild diffuse slowing, predominantly theta range (5-7 Hz) consistent with postictal state. No epileptiform discharges.
Comparable mild background slowing. No focal hemispheric asymmetry greater than left.
No persistent hemispheric dysfunction. No delta-wave asymmetry. No ictal activity. No sharp waves, spike-and-wave, or epileptiform discharges recorded during this session.

eeg.impression: This is an ABNORMAL EEG. Mild diffuse background slowing in the theta range bilaterally, consistent with a post-ictal or encephalopathic state. No interictal epileptiform discharges. No ictal activity or electrographic seizures recorded. No persistent hemispheric asymmetry

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 15 cmH2O. Protein: 0.36 g/L. Glucose: 3.8 mmol/L.

signal_characteristics.FLAIR: marked interval improvement; residual mild cortical signal change only

signal_characteristics.MRA: patent; no change from initial scan

output.impression: Marked interval improvement compared with prior study. Near-complete resolution of left hemispheric cortical swelling and FLAIR signal changes. Sulcal pattern restored. DWI normal throughout — no restricted diffusion. MRA unchanged and patent. The imaging changes were reversible over 72 hours

findings.finding: Patent circle of Willis. No stenosis, occlusion, dissection, or aneurysm.
Patent bilateral internal and external carotid arteries. No dissection. No significant stenosis.

output.impression: Normal MRA head and neck. No stenosis, occlusion, dissection, or aneurysm identified.

output.proposed: combined oral contraceptive (ethinylestradiol 20 mcg + desogestrel) in hemiplegic migraine with motor aura
contraindications: Combined OCP is WHO MEC Category 4 (absolute contraindication) in ALL migraine with aura including hemiplegic subtypes — unacceptable ischaemic stroke risk due to oestrogen-mediated procoagulant state combined with CSD haemodynamic vulnerability
Risk applies to all doses of oestrogen including EE 20 mcg (low-dose) — dose does not mitigate Category 4 classification in hemiplegic migraine
warnings: Combined OCP should not be continued in migraine with aura; progestin-only alternatives (desogestrel 75 mcg, etonogestrel implant) are WHO MEC Category 1 in migraine with aura and are appropriate replacements
No oestrogen-containing preparation is appropriate in any subtype of migraine with aura
alternatives: desogestrel 75 mcg (Cerazette) — progesterone-only pill, WHO MEC Category 1

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass, hydrocephalus, or large-territory infarct.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.
